---
name: horizon-inbox
description: Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create; per-team ownership and read-state; and message other projects or teams via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
---

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- In an agent session, an unqualified list means the **open working queue**, not
  archived history. It is ordered by attention: required protections first,
  unread/direct conversations next, then advisory items. JSON starts with an
  `attention` summary so redirecting stderr cannot erase this signal.
- `horizon inbox show <id> --json` opens exactly one item and marks it read for
  your team. Use `--no-mark-read` for inspection without acknowledgement.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience). A conversation
  may have several recipients; start one with `horizon inbox dm <recipient>...`.
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- A conversation's participants are its recipients **and its initiator**. The
  initiator is recorded as `metadata.started_by`; replies become unread for every
  other participant, including that initiator. Participants are not ownership:
  the initiator remains responsible for deciding when the thread is finished.
- Kinds: `conversation` (a direct/group thread requiring prompt acknowledgement),
  `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),

########## I-0406 [memory] ##########
BLUEPRINT \leanok HAS TWO POSITIONS AND THEY MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS — do not 'fix' a statement-level one because the Lean has a sorry.

Established 2026-07-27 (run 0054, task ajc-truth) by making the mistake and reverting it.

THE RULE. On a STATEMENT environment, \leanok means the signature is formalized. On the
following PROOF environment, it means the proof is formalized. A node whose Lean declaration
is sorry-bodied, or which picks up sorryAx through synthesis, is CORRECTLY marked with
\leanok on the statement and no \leanok on the proof. That is not an overclaim; it is the
convention recording exactly the true state.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I withdrew \leanok from thm:fga_pic_representability and
thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety in AJC because #print axioms at a synthesis site showed sorryAx. A
fresh-context reviewer then found 18 more nodes with the same property and called the audit
inconsistent — correctly, but the resolution was the opposite of what we both assumed. Both
of us had collapsed the two positions into one.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT, for AJC at that date. Of 1553 statement-level \leanok pins,
964 resolve to a declaration that can be probed; 19 of those leak sorryAx; and ZERO of the 19
carries a proof-level \leanok. Meanwhile 156 nodes already use statement-\leanok with a
deliberately unmarked proof. So the blueprint was not overclaiming on this axis at all, and
removing statement-level \leanok would have asserted something false — that no formalized
signature exists.

HOW TO CHECK BEFORE ACTING. Parse statement and proof environments separately and count the
(statement, proof) pairs across the whole blueprint. If (True, False) and (True, noproof) are
common, the project uses the two-position convention and a sorry-bodied declaration under a
statement-level \leanok is fine. Only a PROOF-level \leanok over a sorryAx declaration is a
real defect.

RELATED: a node whose statement claims more than its \lean pin covers IS a real defect (the
convention requires the signature to match). And note the hgraph Lean parser does not resolve
'instance (priority := N) Name', so pinning such an instance produces a spurious 'not found in
Lean sources' warning — pin the plain theorem form instead.

########## I-0408 [memory] ##########
PARALLEL TEAMS SHARE ONE .lake DIRECTORY AND ONE CLI LOCK: a missing .olean, or a horizon-CLI timeout, is often a sibling run in flight rather than a real failure.

Established 2026-07-27 (run 0054, task ajc-truth) with three runs (0053/0054/0055) live on the same project. Written directly to the inbox store because the CLI itself was locked out — see symptom 3.

SYMPTOM 1 — a green file suddenly fails. 'lake env lean scripts/axiom-frontier.lean' failed with "object file '.../Adelic/SectionBounds.olean' of module ... does not exist" on a file that had run green minutes earlier and whose content had not changed. A sibling team was rebuilding that module at that instant, so its .olean was transiently absent from the shared .lake/build tree. Fix: rebuild, then re-run the check. Do NOT conclude a proof or probe is broken on a missing-.olean error while other runs are live.

SYMPTOM 2 — an 8-second check takes many minutes. lake serialises on a shared lock. With 25-30 queued build processes from other runs, a narrow check blocks for a long time. It is waiting, not hung: check 'ps aux | grep "[l]ake build" | wc -l' for queue depth before drawing conclusions, and launch build-then-check as a single backgrounded sequence you then wait on, rather than as two foreground commands that each risk a timeout.

SYMPTOM 3 — horizon CLI writes time out or apply PARTIALLY. The CLI serialises on .archon-horizon/locks/workspace-commit.lock, whose contents are the holder pid — probe it, because a LIVE pid means contention, not a stale lock to clear. Under contention 'roadmap set', 'inbox comment' and 'inbox add' can time out mid-write. Two consequences worth knowing: (a) verify whether a write landed by reading .archon-horizon/roadmap/items/<id>.yaml or .../inbox/local/items/<id>.yaml rather than assuming a timeout meant failure; (b) expect partial application — a single 'roadmap set --summary --owner --pin-commit' landed the summary and silently dropped owner and pin-commit, and repeating it under contention dropped them again. Set one field per call and verify on disk.

THE REPORTING RULE THAT FOLLOWS. Do not carry a green result forward from an earlier run of the same file once the environment has been rebuilt underneath it. Re-run it, or say plainly in the report which run the result came from and that the environment has changed since. Related: [[a-new-module-with-no-importer-looks-green-and-is-invisible]].

########## I-0412 [memory] ##########
GLOBAL GENERATION IN AJC WAS THE CHEAPEST OF THE THREE VANISHING GAPS, NOT THE HARDEST -- it is the equality case of a bound already in the tree.

Established on ajc-rr run 0055 session 0004; landed as AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean, sorry-free, kernel-checked, all 14 keystones [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

THE MISRANKING. Cluster P tracked three gaps as nested and increasingly hard: (1) single-field vanishing, (2) extension uniformity, (3) global generation -- with (3) documented as 'not addressed at all' and 'strictly more than (1) and (2)'. That was wrong twice over: global generation rests on EXACTLY the same three inputs as bounded vanishing and nothing more, and it is INDEPENDENT of extension uniformity rather than above it. Extension uniformity is the genuinely hard one and is still untouched.

WHY IT WAS CHEAP, which is the reusable part. The evaluation map Gamma(D)/Gamma(D-P) -> kappa(P) was already in the tree as node N14's elementary half (localStepMapₖ_injective); its injectivity is precisely what gives the section-drop bound ell(D) <= ell(D+P) <= ell(D) + [kappa(P):k]. Global generation is that bound's EQUALITY CASE. Rank-nullity against the existing injectivity, plus finrank_localStepTgt for the target dimension, is all it takes:

  ell(D) - ell(D-P) = [kappa(P):k] + h1(D) - h1(D-P)

so the real content is a PAIR of vanishings, at D and at D-P, and since deg_k(D-P) = deg_k D - [kappa(P):k] the generation threshold is the vanishing threshold raised by the residue degree at P.

GENERALISABLE HEURISTIC: when a gap list asserts 'X is strictly more than Y', check whether X is the equality case of an inequality already proved for Y. Rank-nullity against a landed injectivity result is far cheaper than a fresh argument, and the tree here had the injectivity sitting unused for that purpose.

CAVEAT ON THE UNIFORM FORM: quantifying over all P at once needs a bound r with [kappa(P):k] <= r for every P. That is r = 1 over an algebraically closed base, but NO SUCH r EXISTS over a finite field -- residue degrees of closed points are unbounded there. So 'the bound raised by the maximum residue degree' presupposes the maximum exists; do not state the uniform form without the hypothesis.

SECOND RESULT, same session: residueDeg = 1 is no longer prose. Proved equivalent to a first-order approximation statement in the order language (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues), then that statement discharged for an algebraically closed base from the stalk residue field (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed). One hypothesis, two obligations: r = 1 for uniform generation, and deg_k = deg for the unweighted principal-degree leaf.

########## I-0430 [memory] ##########
[persistent] A `Function.Surjective ⇑d` statement crosses a propositionally-equal family for FREE — no congruence helper

Established by auditing ajc-gate run 0053 s0006. `Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean:178-184` (correction 4) predicted that moving Čech surjectivity from the family `π_A ≫ p` to `q` would need a `subst`-style congruence helper, because "the module structures sit inside the *type* of `moduleSectionDiffBase`" and a naive `rw` would hit "motive is not type correct". **That prediction was wrong, and the reason generalises.**

- `Function.Surjective ⇑d` mentions only the *underlying function* of `d`. The `Γ(S,⊤)`-module structures are instance arguments of the `LinearMap`, so two `moduleSectionDiffBase`s that differ only in them are the **same proposition**, not merely equivalent ones.
- Combined with `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff_pushforward` being `rfl`, this let `Picard/RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange.lean:213-217` write `have hd : Function.Surjective ⇑((𝒰.preimage π_A).moduleSectionDiffBase q L) := hengine.1` where `hengine.1` is stated for `𝒰`, `p` and `(π_A)_* L`. One `exact`, zero transport.

**Rule.** Before writing a transport lemma across a propositional equality of morphisms, check whether the target statement is `Prop`-valued in the *carrier* only (`Surjective`, `Injective`, `= 0` of an application). If so, try `exact` first. Transport is genuinely needed only when the linear/`Module` structure itself appears in the conclusion (e.g. `Module.Flat`, `LinearEquiv`, `ker … |>.FG`).

/-! §2b The SEVENTH trap, and the one that is hardest to defend against: a hypothesis the
project can REFUTE.

Trap (c) below is a named hypothesis that is false as stated — someone has to notice that it
is false. This is the sharper version: a hypothesis whose negation is *derivable from
declarations already in the tree*, so the project simultaneously proves `H → C` and, at every
instance anyone would use, `¬H`. The theorem is true, axiom-clean, non-vacuous by every probe
in this file, and empty.

Measured instance (2026-07-28, `RiemannRoch/Adelic/LedgerClosure.lean`): `chi_eq_of_bump`
takes `hbump : ∀ P E, χ(1·P + E) = χ(E) + residueDeg P`. Iterating it down the anti-effective
cone forces `χ(-m·P) = χ(0) - m·[κ(P):k]`, and since `χ = ℓ - h¹` with `ℓ ≥ 0`, `h¹` must grow
linearly there. So `hbump` is FALSE on every cover whose `h¹` is bounded — and outright false
at the degenerate cover `U₀ = U₁ = ⊤`, where the Čech `H¹` vanishes identically, as soon as a
single prime divisor exists. That refutation needs no exactness data at all. A weaker,
conditional refutation is available at each prime outside the overlap `U₀ ∩ U₁`, where
`A(1·P + E) = A(E)` makes the local step a subsingleton and the χ-jump `0`.

So the honest status of `hbump` is: consistent; refutable at `U₀ = U₁ = ⊤` given one prime
divisor; refutable on every bounded-`h¹` cover; and satisfiable only on covers whose `h¹` is
unbounded on the anti-effective cone. None of that contradicts the vanishing lane, whose
results are high-degree only — which is exactly why nobody noticed.

What defeats each check, in order: `#print axioms` sees a clean line; a consistency witness
exists (`bump_of_isEmpty_primeDivisor`, on a scheme with no prime divisors); an elaboration
probe synthesises every binder; and non-vacuity in the trap-(c) sense holds, because the
hypothesis is not contradictory — it is merely refutable where it is wanted. The only check
that finds it is reading the PRODUCER's side conditions and asking whether the family the
hypothesis quantifies over contains members where the tree proves the negation.

So the discipline this adds to the other six: for a hypothesis quantified over a family, do
not stop at "is it satisfiable". Ask where the project can derive its negation. Recorded as
I-0449/I-0454 with the machine-checked steps, and as the durable lesson I-0451.

§2c The EIGHTH, found in the same audit and cheaper to check than any of the others: a
hypothesis EQUIVALENT to the conclusion it is supposed to buy.

`chi_eq_of_bump` proves `hbump → closed χ-ledger`. The converse is three lines —
`rw [hledger (pointDivisor P + E), hledger E, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring` — because
`degK` is an `AddMonoidHom` and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A → B` whose
converse is trivial transports no information: it is a restatement, and "is `A` satisfiable"
is literally the question "is `B` satisfiable". The theorem is true, axiom-clean,
instantiable, non-vacuous, and not a reduction.

This is the re-indexing failure mode one level out, and it is the one to check FIRST, because
it costs a single `rw` attempt: before believing that `H → C` reduces `C` to `H`, try to prove
`C → H`. If that succeeds, no amount of axiom-probing will tell you the result is empty.
